<a id="llm-recipe"></a>

## LLM Recipe

**Editorial synthesis:** The selected work connects data quality and architecture to a staged training process: broad pretraining, targeted continuation, adaptation, preference learning, and reasoning reinforcement learning. Current directions include synthetic training data, efficient hybrid expert models, architecture-aware context extension, and interpretable post-training interventions. Open recipes make individual choices easier to inspect, but improvements should be compared under the same data, total compute, evaluation protocol, and downstream task.

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

Data filtering, deduplication, mixtures, synthetic data, quality and tokenizers.

#### [It's All Training: A Fully Synthetic Single-Stage Recipe for LLMs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37891>)

SYNTH turns curated Wikipedia seeds into grounded questions, reasoning traces, and varied tasks, allowing small language models to acquire instruction-following behavior within a single training stage. Controlled data ablations make it a useful reference for testing whether carefully generated synthetic data can improve learning efficiency and targeted factual recall.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T03:57:00Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Synthetic Data, Pretraining, Small Models

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37891>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3-5 describe generation and matched 600M-model data ablations; the authors report an 11-17 point advantage over their post-trained web-data controls across the aggregate task groups.

**Limitations:** Knowledge is bounded by roughly 58,000 seed articles, language coverage is shaped by English sources, and experiments target small models; token savings are not equivalent to total savings once teacher generation is counted.

### 1.2 Model Architecture &amp; Scaling Laws

Transformers, MoE, SSM/hybrid architectures and model/data/compute allocation.

#### [Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653>)

Kimi K3 combines hybrid recurrent and latent attention, attention across residual layers, and a sparse expert architecture in a native multimodal model with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion activated parameters. Its public report connects architecture, data, optimization, and long-context post-training, providing a current reference for how several efficiency improvements support scaling a large open-weight model.

**Published:** 2026-07-27 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** MoE, Hybrid Attention, Scaling Laws, Multimodal

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24653>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The August 7 revision includes architecture equations, scaling-law experiments, training schedules, and evaluation settings; Section 3.2 reports approximately 2.5x overall scaling efficiency relative to Kimi K2 on held-out validation data.

**Limitations:** The efficiency result combines multiple changes and is not an isolated architectural gain; the authors state that overall performance trails their strongest proprietary comparators, and released weights do not make the full training process reproducible.

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

Objectives, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes and training stability.

#### [Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534>)

Kimi K2 introduces MuonClip, which adds query/key weight clipping to Muon so that attention logits remain controlled during large-scale mixture-of-experts training. It is a practical optimization reference because it links a specific instability mechanism to an intervention used in a trillion-parameter training run.

**Published:** 2025-07-28 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Muon, Optimization, Training Stability, MoE

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.20534>) · [Project](<https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K2>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The optimizer algorithm, mid-scale instability experiment, and Appendix D ablations accompany the authors' report of training on 15.5 trillion tokens without observed loss spikes.

**Limitations:** This is an established recipe component, not a current model ranking; the trillion-parameter evidence is author-reported, and the intervention needs attention-specific adaptation and threshold choices.

### 1.4 Mid-training &amp; Continual Learning

Domain continued pretraining, context extension, continual learning and forgetting.

#### [Olmo 3](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13961>)

Olmo 3 releases an end-to-end model development pipeline with separate pretraining, targeted mid-training, context extension, and post-training stages, together with data and intermediate checkpoints. Its short continuation experiments and integration tests provide a reproducible way to choose data mixtures and measure capability tradeoffs before committing to a full training run.

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The April 14, 2026 paper revision documents stage-level comparisons, data filtering, continuation ablations, and domain tradeoffs; public code and checkpoints make it a useful open training reference.

**Limitations:** Recipe development focuses on 7B and 32B models, with substantial compute requirements; improvements on one data domain can reduce performance on others, and release-time leadership claims are not treated as current rankings.

#### [Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension](<https://allenai.org/papers/olmpool>)

OlmPool holds data and context-extension procedures fixed across 26 comparable models to test how normalization, grouped-query attention, sliding windows, and pretraining context length affect later long-context ability. The results show why a context-extension recipe should be validated on the intended architecture early, since ordinary short-context metrics can miss substantial downstream weaknesses.

**Limitations:** The controlled suite centers on approximately 7B dense models and one data/extension setup; these findings do not establish that the same architectural choices are universally harmful at other scales or training budgets.

### 1.5 Supervised Fine-tuning &amp; Adaptation

Instruction tuning, SFT data and mixtures, LoRA and parameter-efficient adaptation.

#### [LoRA Without Regret](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora/>)

This experimental study examines when low-rank adaptation can match full fine-tuning by varying adapter rank, training-set size, batch size, learning rate, and the layers being adapted. It gives practitioners a concrete recipe for efficient adaptation, including sufficient adapter capacity and coverage of feed-forward layers, while identifying large-data and large-batch regimes where gaps remain.

### 1.6 Preference Alignment &amp; Reward Modeling

Preference datasets, DPO-like methods, reward models and process supervision.

#### [Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290>)

Direct Preference Optimization converts a regularized preference-learning objective into a direct loss on preferred and rejected responses, avoiding a separately trained reward model and online policy rollouts. It remains a useful foundational baseline for aligning model behavior from offline preference pairs with a comparatively simple training pipeline.

**Limitations:** Its preference-model assumptions and dependence on offline data matter; the original experiments do not establish universal superiority to online RL or robustness under distribution shift.

### 1.7 Reinforcement Learning &amp; Reasoning

RLHF, RLVR, policy optimization, reasoning training, tool use and multi-turn agent RL.

#### [DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948>)

DeepSeek-R1 demonstrates large-scale reasoning training with group-relative policy optimization and verifiable rewards, while separating a pure-RL experiment from a staged recipe that improves response usability. It supplies a foundational reference for eliciting reasoning from a strong pretrained model and transferring those capabilities to smaller models through distillation.

**Limitations:** Reliable verifiers are central, model-based rewards can be exploited, and the reported model has overthinking, language-mixing, structured-output, and tool-use limitations; this is a foundational recipe rather than a current leaderboard claim.

### 1.8 Distillation &amp; Model Compression

Knowledge/reasoning distillation, pruning, quantization algorithms and model merging.

#### [On-Policy Distillation](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/on-policy-distillation/>)

On-policy distillation lets a student generate its own trajectories and uses teacher token probabilities to provide dense feedback on the states the student actually visits. The report demonstrates a practical route to improving reasoning and restoring instruction-following after domain training without rebuilding an entire reinforcement-learning reward pipeline.

### 1.9 Test-Time Scaling &amp; Inference Algorithms

Inference-time search, verification, reranking and adaptive reasoning budgets.

#### [s1: Simple test-time scaling](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393>)

s1 combines supervised training on a small curated reasoning dataset with budget forcing, which controls when a model stops or continues its thinking at inference time. Its simple open implementation separates training quality from inference-time computation, making it a useful baseline for studying the accuracy and cost tradeoff of longer reasoning.

**Published:** 2025-01-31 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Test-Time Scaling, Reasoning, Budget Control

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393>) · [Code](<https://github.com/simplescaling/s1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The March 1 revision includes data-selection ablations, decoding comparisons, and compute-versus-accuracy curves; the authors report AIME 2024 accuracy increasing from 50% to 57% under budget forcing.

**Limitations:** The principal evidence comes from a small set of math and science benchmarks; gains eventually flatten and are bounded by context length, so more thinking is not a guarantee of more reliable answers.

### 1.10 Model Evaluation, Safety &amp; Interpretability

Capability evaluation, contamination, generalization, robustness, safety and mechanistic understanding.

#### [Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12360>)

This work uses interpretable model features to identify which concepts preference data rewards or suppresses before optimization, then connects those signals to targeted data and training interventions. It offers a way to debug unwanted changes such as safety regressions and excessive stylistic habits at their training source instead of relying only on aggregate scores after training.

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The June 11 revision tests feature-based predictions against observed training changes and compares intervention protocols; the reported feature-conditioned prediction fit reaches R-squared 0.9 in the studied setup.

**Limitations:** Concept extraction and correlations constrain what can be diagnosed; the paper observes off-target effects for several interventions, so interpretability does not provide a general guarantee of safe post-training.

<a id="ai-agent-dev"></a>

## AI Agent Dev

**Editorial synthesis:** Agent capability depends on the combination of a model, its interaction loop, tools, context, and execution environment. Durable patterns include reasoning-action loops, model-oriented interfaces, retrieval, persistent progress records, and task-specific evaluation; recent work explores learned harnesses, retrospective skill learning, and more deliberate allocation of inference effort. Multi-agent execution is useful when work can be divided, while success, cost, recovery behavior, and resistance to untrusted instructions require separate measurement.

### 2.1 Agent Architecture &amp; Planning

Agent loops, task decomposition, planning, reflection and execution control.

#### [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>)

ReAct alternates reasoning, environment actions, and observations so an agent can revise its plan using external evidence. It remains a useful foundation for tool-using agent loops because task execution and information gathering become part of the reasoning process.

**Published:** 2022-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Tool Use, Grounding

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629>) · [Project](<https://react-lm.github.io/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ysymyth/ReAct>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The ICLR camera-ready paper compares reasoning-only, acting-only and interleaved policies on question answering, fact verification and interactive tasks; its ablations and failure analysis make the control pattern inspectable. The arXiv history records v1 on October 6, 2022 and v3 on March 10, 2023.

**Limitations:** This is a foundational method, not a claim of current benchmark leadership. Retrieval failures and repetitive loops remain possible; ReAct alone trails chain-of-thought on the reported HotpotQA setting.

#### [Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

This work separates task execution from a controller that assesses accumulated work, proposes next steps, evaluates their value, and dispatches workers using persistent artifact memory. It offers a way to spend larger inference budgets more effectively on long tasks by choosing which partial results to reuse, repair, or abandon.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Planning, Test-Time Scaling, Memory, Long-Horizon

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3, 5 and 6 provide the controller design and matched-worker comparisons across four benchmarks and three models; reported ProgramBench performance is 71.5% with GPT-5.5 versus 58.0% for Codex. Submission history verifies September 29, 2026 at 17:57:25 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint with no independent reproduction here. Equal model-call allowances do not equal token, latency or FLOP budgets; control overhead hurts at small budgets, and the design underperforms direct control on the LongCoT-mini chess subset.

These patterns help long-running agents retain decisions and recover relevant information without carrying every prior observation in the active prompt.

#### [Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516>)

Search-R1 trains language models to alternate reasoning with search queries, using answer-level rewards and masking retrieved passages out of the policy loss. It provides an open recipe for learning when and how to obtain external evidence instead of relying only on a fixed retrieval step before answering.

AgentDojo provides an extensible environment for testing whether tool-using agents complete legitimate tasks while resisting instructions embedded in untrusted tool results. The accessible repository supports extension; arXiv records June 19, 2024 for v1 and November 24, 2024 for the inspected v3.

**Limitations:** The original scores concern historical models and the included environments, not current deployment security. Tool filtering can fail when required tools also enable an attack; the original suite does not cover continuing user tasks with an unreset context.

#### [Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35732>)

Failure-Transparent Agents isolates a reporting problem by giving models fixed failed-tool traces and checking whether subsequent claims are supported by the available evidence. Its structured evidence contract offers a concrete design to test when reducing false completion claims, while preserving useful recovery advice.

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The benchmark includes 100 synthetic blocked tasks and 3,600 human-annotated responses across six models; authors report pooled false-success rates of 22.8% for baseline and 0.8% with the contract. Submission history verifies September 28, 2026 at 17:51:41 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint measuring response fidelity after fixed failures, not end-to-end execution or recovery. The contract bundles multiple changes, the additional model cohort is post-confirmatory, and independent double annotation or inter-annotator agreement is not reported.

<a id="ai-training-inference-infra"></a>

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

**Editorial synthesis:** Training systems combine several forms of parallelism, while reinforcement learning adds a changing balance between generation and policy updates. Serving systems manage batching, prefill and decoding, cache reuse, and memory placement; recent work pushes attention kernels, cache compression, and low-precision learning further. Hardware, interconnects, and checkpointing determine whether local improvements survive at system scale, so kernel throughput, training throughput, and end-to-end application performance should be compared separately.

### 3.1 Distributed Training Systems

Data/tensor/pipeline/expert/context parallelism, sharding and communication overlap.

#### [Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04473>)

Megatron-LM combines tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, using interleaved pipeline stages and communication optimizations to distribute very large models across GPU clusters. It provides a foundational framework for choosing a parallelism configuration by balancing model memory, communication, and time spent waiting between pipeline stages.

**Published:** 2021-04-09 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Distributed Training, Tensor Parallelism, Pipeline Parallelism

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04473>) · [Code](<https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The SC 2021 paper analyzes parallelism and microbatch tradeoffs, then benchmarks training iterations for models up to one trillion parameters on as many as 3,072 A100 GPUs; component experiments examine communication and pipeline scheduling.

**Limitations:** These are historical systems measurements, not current hardware rankings or proof that a trillion-parameter model was trained to convergence. The best configuration depends on cluster topology, model shape, and batch size.

#### [DCP: Addressing Input Dynamism In Long-Context Training via Dynamic Context Parallelism](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10620>)

Dynamic Context Parallelism partitions attention into small blocks and replans their placement for each batch's sequence lengths and attention masks. It reduces unnecessary cross-GPU communication and balances variable-length workloads, making long-context training more efficient when static parallelism wastes resources.

**Published:** 2025-10-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Context Parallelism, Long Context, Distributed Training

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10620>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper provides a hypergraph-based planner, execution design, attention microbenchmarks, and end-to-end 8B-model experiments on 64 A100 GPUs; reported training speedups reach 1.16x for causal masks and 1.46x for sparse masks.

**Limitations:** The causal-mask range includes 0.94x slowdowns; benefits depend on sequence variability, mask sparsity, planning resources, and communication overlap. Public implementation was not verified.

### 3.2 RL &amp; Rollout Infrastructure

Distributed rollouts, asynchronous RL, generation/training coordination and weight synchronization.

#### [AReaL: A Large-Scale Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning System for Language Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24298>)

AReaL separates rollout generation from policy updates so workers can keep producing and consuming training data without waiting for the longest response in a batch. Staleness control and a modified policy objective help retain learning quality while improving GPU utilization, providing an open reference for asynchronous reasoning-model reinforcement learning.

**Published:** 2025-05-30 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Asynchronous RL, Rollouts, Policy Staleness

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24298>) · [Code](<https://github.com/areal-project/AReaL>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The authors evaluate mathematical and code reasoning across 1.5B–32B models and ablate policy staleness and interruptible generation; the original experiments report up to 2.57x throughput versus synchronous configurations.

**Limitations:** The gains depend on balancing generation and training; short generations can reduce the advantage, and excessive policy staleness still harms learning. Results are author-reported and software-version specific.

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

Request scheduling, continuous batching, prefill/decode disaggregation and elastic serving.

#### [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180>)

PagedAttention stores key-value caches in dynamically allocated blocks, allowing vLLM to avoid large contiguous reservations and share cached state across related sequences. More efficient memory use permits larger concurrent batches, making this a foundational open reference for high-throughput language-model serving.

**Published:** 2023-09-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Serving, PagedAttention, Memory Management

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180>) · [Code](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper details cache management, scheduling, preemption, and distributed execution, with OPT and LLaMA experiments on A100 GPUs using ShareGPT- and Alpaca-derived workloads plus block-size ablations.

**Limitations:** The original comparisons use historical FasterTransformer and reimplemented Orca baselines with synthetic arrival times. Block size trades memory fragmentation against kernel efficiency; the paper does not rank current serving releases.

#### [SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104>)

SGLang combines a programming interface for multi-call language-model workflows with a runtime that reuses prompt prefixes through RadixAttention and accelerates constrained decoding. This reduces repeated prefill work and exposes parallelism in agent, retrieval, and structured-output applications, making it a useful open serving reference.

**Published:** 2023-12-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Serving, Prefix Caching, Structured Outputs

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The revised paper studies 7B–70B language models and multimodal workloads on A10G/A100 hardware, with component ablations and cache-hit measurements that explain the observed improvements.

**Limitations:** The historical comparison uses vLLM 0.2.5 and other older baselines; its headline speedup is not a ranking of current engines. Long-output workloads with little shared context show much smaller gains.

#### [DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670>)

DistServe runs prompt prefill and token decoding on separate GPUs and independently chooses their resource allocations and parallelism. It increases the number of requests served within both first-token and per-token latency targets, establishing a practical foundation for disaggregated inference.

**Published:** 2024-01-18 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Prefill Decode Disaggregation, Serving, Latency SLO

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670>) · [Code](<https://github.com/LLMServe/DistServe>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The OSDI work evaluates OPT-13B/66B/175B across chat, code, and summarization workloads on 32 A100 GPUs, with bandwidth-aware placement and ablations of the disaggregation design.

**Limitations:** Results use historical engines, synthetic arrival times, and workload-specific latency targets. KV transfers need sufficient bandwidth, and the prototype leaves advanced preemption and fault tolerance to future work.

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

Attention execution, KV management/reuse, offloading and long-context memory efficiency.

#### [LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09665>)

LMCache makes KV caches reusable across requests and inference engines through a separate storage layer, optimized transfers, and a standardized connector. It lets serving systems trade GPU memory and repeated prefill computation for CPU or remote storage while also supporting prefill-decode disaggregation.

**Published:** 2025-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** KV Cache, Offloading, Distributed Storage

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09665>) · [Code](<https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The revised report evaluates CPU offload, remote storage, and disaggregated serving with multiple open models on H100 hardware, including real-trace-derived workloads and transfer-level ablations.

**Limitations:** Cache reuse depends on exact shared context and available bandwidth; remote retrieval can be slower than recomputation. Reported gains depend on the compared engine versions, and SGLang's native CPU offload performs similarly in one tested configuration.

#### [DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19969>)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer cache reuse, sparse attention, FP4 KV storage, and approximate replay of sliding-window states to shrink long-context memory. Its encoder-decoder design also reduces prefill work, targeting the memory, storage, and bandwidth costs of input-heavy agents with up to one million context tokens.

**Limitations:** These are architecture-specific author measurements, not universal savings. Bounded replay reconstructs approximate states; the authors identify uncharacterized robustness risks at cache-resumption boundaries and in sparse long-context retrieval.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

GPU kernels, operator fusion, compilation, execution graphs and hardware adaptation.

#### [FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05451>)

FlashAttention-4 redesigns attention pipelines for Blackwell GPUs, overlapping matrix operations with softmax while reducing shared-memory traffic and other non-matrix overhead. The CuTe-DSL implementation provides an open example of how attention algorithms and kernels must adapt when compute throughput grows faster than supporting hardware.

**Published:** 2026-03-05 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Attention Kernels, Blackwell, CuTe DSL

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05451>) · [Code](<https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/tree/main/flash_attn/cute>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. B200 BF16 attention benchmarks span 1K–32K sequences, causal and noncausal masks, and several head dimensions; the authors report up to 1.3x over cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7x over the tested Triton baseline.

**Limitations:** These are attention-kernel measurements, not full-model training speedups. The paper explicitly notes that newer cuDNN releases incorporated similar techniques and achieved comparable performance; gains are hardware- and shape-specific.

### 3.6 Low-Precision &amp; Efficient Execution

FP8/FP4/INT execution, quantized kernels, sparse compute and speculative decoding systems.

#### [Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22870>)

This study traces instability in FP8 reinforcement learning to quantization errors that distort policy-update clipping and prevent undesirable outputs from receiving corrective gradients. Its Calibrated Clipping method periodically uses BF16 reference statistics to adjust clipping bounds, making low-precision rollout and training more stable across the tested reasoning models.

**Published:** 2026-09-19 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** FP8, Reinforcement Learning, Numerical Stability

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22870>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. GRPO and DAPO experiments cover 8B–32B Qwen models and multiple FP8 scaling granularities, with controlled analyses of entropy surges and recovery toward BF16 performance.

**Limitations:** Periodic calibration requires two BF16 shadow forward passes. Reported 1.1–1.5x throughput measurements isolate offline training and exclude calibration, so they do not establish end-to-end RL speedups; some accuracy gaps remain and code was not verified.

### 3.7 Data Pipelines, Storage &amp; Checkpointing

Data loading, storage throughput, distributed checkpoints, recovery and fault tolerance.

#### [6x faster Async Checkpointing in PyTorch, using Cached Plans, no GIL contention](<https://pytorch.org/blog/6x-faster-async-checkpointing/>)

PyTorch distributed checkpointing moves background saving into a separate process and reuses save plans to reduce Python lock contention and expensive metadata collectives. These changes keep checkpoint persistence from depressing training throughput for as long, making frequent recovery checkpoints more affordable at large GPU counts.

**Published:** 2025-04-30 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Checkpointing, Fault Tolerance, PyTorch

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Blog](<https://pytorch.org/blog/6x-faster-async-checkpointing/>) · [Code](<https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/distributed/checkpoint/state_dict_saver.py>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Meta and Crusoe report a Llama-3-70B/TorchTitan run on 1,856 H200 GPUs where background checkpoint processing fell from about 436 to 67 seconds, with GPU-to-CPU staging taking about 0.78 seconds.

**Limitations:** The 6.5x figure concerns background checkpoint processing, not overall model training. Benefit depends on storage, checkpoint structure, and repeated plans; initial planning and coordinator metadata remain costs.

### 3.8 Hardware, Networking &amp; Cluster Efficiency

Accelerators, interconnects, cluster scheduling, profiling, utilization, cost and energy.

#### [Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09343>)

This infrastructure study connects DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts architecture, low-precision execution, and communication needs to the design of its GPU cluster and multi-plane network. It provides a concrete reference for reasoning about how accelerator features, interconnect topology, and model design jointly determine training and serving efficiency.
